inflectere: inflectō, -ere, -flexī, -flexum — to bend, turn aside, sway, change (pres. inf.)
invita: invītus, -a, -um — unwilling, reluctant, against one's will (f. nom. sg., Iūnō speaking)
iubeas: iubeō, -ēre, iussī, iussum — to order, bid, command (2nd sg. pres. subj.)
iungent: iungō, -ere, iūnxī, iūnctum — to join, link, unite; make (a treaty) (3rd pl. fut. ind.)
iuturnam: Iūturna, -ae (f.) — Juturna, Turnus's sister, a water-nymph (acc. sg.)

lege: lēx, lēgis (f.) — law, rule, condition, decree (abl. sg.)
lentoque: lentus, -a, -um — tough, pliant, clinging, slow (m./n. abl. sg., with stirpe/rōbore) + -que 'and'
licere: licet, -ēre, licuit — it is allowed, it is permitted (impers.; pres. inf., in indirect statement)
lignum: lignum, -ī (n.) — wood, timber, tree trunk, stock (nom./acc. sg.)
luctans: luctor, -ārī, -ātus sum — to wrestle, struggle, strive (pres. part., m. nom. sg., deponent)
ludicra: lūdicrus, -a, -um — playful, of sport; n. as noun, a plaything, game (n. nom. pl.)
maiestate: māiestās, -ātis (f.) — majesty, dignity, greatness, grandeur (abl. sg.)
minitans: minitor, -ārī, -ātus sum — to threaten repeatedly, menace (pres. part., m. nom. sg., deponent)
mixtum: misceō, -ēre, miscuī, mixtum — to mix, blend, mingle (perf. pass. part., n. nom. sg., with genus)

occideritque: occidō, -ere, -cidī, -cāsum — to fall, perish, die (3rd sg. fut. perf. ind.) + -que 'and'

pinnae: pinna, -ae (f.) — feather; feathers strung on a line to scare game (gen. sg.; formīdine pinnae, the feather-scare)
praesensque: praesēns, -entis — present, at hand, in person; resolute (m. nom. sg.) + -que 'and'

procurrit: prōcurrō, -ere, -(cu)currī, -cursum — to run forward, rush out, dash ahead (3rd sg. pres. ind.)
profanos: profānus, -a, -um — unholy, unhallowed, profane (m. acc. pl., with quōs)
puniceae: pūniceus, -a, -um — crimson, scarlet, purple-red (f. gen. sg., with pinnae)
puro: pūrus, -a, -um — clean, clear, unobstructed, open (m./n. abl. sg., with campō)
recursent: recursō, -āre, -āvī — to run back, come back again, recur (3rd pl. pres. subj.)
recusant: recūsō, -āre, -āvī, -ātum — to refuse, decline, reject (3rd pl. pres. ind.)
refecti: reficiō, -ere, -fēcī, -fectum — to remake, restore, refresh, revive (perf. pass. part., m. nom. pl.)
repertor: repertor, -ōris (m.) — discoverer, inventor, author, founder (nom. sg.)
responsant: respōnsō, -āre — to answer back, echo, resound (3rd pl. pres. ind.)
retexunt: retexō, -ere, -texuī, -textum — to unweave, undo; go back over, retrace (3rd pl. pres. ind.)
ritusque: ritus, -ūs (m.) — rite, ceremony, custom, usage (acc. pl.) + -que 'and'
roboris: rōbur, rōboris (n.) — hard oak, oak wood; strength, toughness (gen. sg.)
saeptum: saepiō, -īre, saepsī, saeptum — to hedge in, fence, enclose, pen (perf. pass. part., m. acc. sg., with cervum)
saturnique: Sāturnus, -ī (m.) — Saturn, father of Jupiter, Juno and Neptune (m. gen. sg.) + -que 'and'
similisque: similis, -e — like, similar, resembling (m. nom. sg.; + gen./dat.) + -que 'and'
starem: stō, stāre, stetī, statum — to stand, stand firm, hold position (1st sg. impf. subj.)
suasi: suādeō, -ēre, suāsī, suāsum — to advise, urge, persuade (+ dat.) (1st sg. perf. ind.)
submisso: submittō, -ere, -mīsī, -missum — to let down, lower, humble (perf. pass. part., m./n. abl. sg., with vultū)

subsident: subsīdō, -ere, -sēdī, -sessum — to settle down, sink, sink down, remain (3rd pl. fut. ind.)
suspendere: suspendō, -ere, -pendī, -pēnsum — to hang up, suspend, dedicate by hanging (pres. inf.)
sustulerant: tollō, -ere, sustulī, sublātum — to lift up, raise, carry off, take away (3rd pl. pluperf. ind.)
tardata: tardō, -āre, -āvī, -ātum — to slow down, delay, hinder (perf. pass. part., f. abl. sg., with sagittā)
tenenti: teneō, -ēre, tenuī, tentum — to hold, grasp, keep (pres. part., m. dat. sg.; as noun, one who holds)
terretque: terreō, -ēre, terruī, territum — to frighten, scare, terrify (3rd sg. pres. ind.) + -que 'and'
traheremque: trahō, -ere, trāxī, tractum — to drag, draw, pull along (1st sg. impf. subj.) + -que 'and'
ulterius: ulterior, -ius — farther, more distant; ulterius (adv.), further, any further, beyond (n. acc. sg. as adv.)
umber: Umber, -bra, -brum — Umbrian, of Umbria; Umber (m. nom. sg. as noun), an Umbrian hound
valeret: valeō, -ēre, valuī — to be strong, have power, avail (3rd sg. impf. subj.)
vestros: vester, vestra, vestrum — your (pl. poss.) (m. acc. pl., with honōrēs)
veto: vetō, -āre, vetuī, vetitum — to forbid, prohibit, ban (1st sg. pres. ind.)
victusque: vincō, -ere, vīcī, victum — to conquer, defeat (perf. pass. part., m. nom. sg.) + -que 'and'
violari: violō, -āre, -āvī, -ātum — to injure, outrage, wound, profane (pres. pass. inf.)
vividus: vīvidus, -a, -um — lively, vigorous, full of life, spirited (m. nom. sg.)
volensque: volō, velle, voluī — to wish, be willing (pres. part., m. nom. sg.; volēns, willing) + -que 'and'
voluitque: volō, velle, voluī — to wish, want, be willing (3rd sg. perf. ind.) + -que 'and'
volvis: volvō, -ere, volvī, volūtum — to roll, turn over, revolve, ponder (2nd sg. pres. ind.)
votas: vōveō, -ēre, vōvī, vōtum — to vow, promise to a god, dedicate (perf. pass. part., f. acc. pl., with vestēs)
